claims.text: In 2021-2025, age-standardised cancer mortality in South Ostrobothnia wellbeing services county was 4.8% above the national level (ratio 1.048, 95% interval 1.012-1.085), about 24.6 more deaths a year than its age structure predicts.

Referrals for specialised health care received processed within 3 days, % of referrals received: South Ostrobothnia wellbeing services county is at 70.8 (three-year mean to 2025) against 76.8 nationally.
Among the stages that public data can measure, the earliest one where South Ostrobothnia wellbeing services county is clearly worse than the country is referral into specialist care.

Time from referral to diagnosis and from diagnosis to first treatment is not published by county for any cancer, so the Goal 3 indicator "patients access treatment within the established target times" cannot be checked from open data.

Recommended: standardised, timed cancer pathways with a fast-track referral. Under the stated assumptions this postpones about 9.4 deaths a year in South Ostrobothnia wellbeing services county (range 1.4-18.9) for an assumed EUR 284,211 a year; it stayed in the portfolio in 94% of sensitivity runs.

Proportion of invited to colorectal cancer screening who attended, %: 75.6% against the 80% target. Reminder and multilingual re-invitation for colorectal screening is expected to add 1.5-4.37 percentage points, closing about 69% of the gap.
First step for every county: Add first contact, referral, diagnosis and first treatment dates, plus entry route, to the national cancer quality register and publish county-level medians quarterly.
